mainTopic: The rules of פסק (רבי יוסי vs. רבי יהודה, and רב משרשיא's statement), and whether a נכרי's objects acquire שביתה, applied to the case of the rams in מברכתא.
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא. רבי יוסי says a כהן may leave ארץ ישראל to learn תורה from the teacher who suits him, and he backs this with the story of יוסף הכהן going to צידן. רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יוסי. The גמרא asks why this ruling was needed, and אביי answers that it extends the general rule to disputes found in a ברייתא. The גמרא then concludes that רב משרשיא only meant that the rules of פסק are not accepted by everyone, since רב did not follow them. Next, שמואל rules that a נכרי's objects do not acquire שביתה. After a challenge from a ברייתא, the גמרא places שמואל with the רבנן and explains that he is teaching that there is no גזירה. רבי יוחנן disagrees and holds that there is such a גזירה. In a practical case about rams brought to מברכתא, רבא first ruled leniently. רבינא challenged him, since the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן, so רבא allowed only the people of מברכתא to buy them. The amud ends with the start of רבי חייא's ברייתא about a water-filled ditch between two תחומי שבת, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's reason: not every teacher is right for every student
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes רבי יוסי's reasoning: a כהן may leave ארץ ישראל to learn תורה because a person does not succeed in learning from just anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because a person does not merit to learn from everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the ברייתא in the middle. רבי יוסי explains why a כהן may leave ארץ ישראל to learn תורה even if teachers are available at home: not every teacher works for every student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה held that a כהן should only leave if he has nowhere to learn in ארץ ישראל. רבי יוסי allows it even when there are teachers at home, because the right teacher for this student may live abroad. This is the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי that the rest of this passage builds on.
steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts mid-sentence. The 'because' explains רבי יוסי's lenient opinion, which allows a כהן to leave ארץ ישראל to learn even when local teachers exist. It is not a general statement on its own.

phrases.english: For not from everyone
phrases.notes: Continues רבי יוסי's opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: does a person merit to learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין מִן הַכֹּל זוֹכֶה אָדָם לִלְמוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous amud (47a), where רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about a כהן leaving ארץ ישראל to learn תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, a כהן may leave ארץ ישראל to learn תורה even if teachers are available there, since a person cannot learn well from every teacher.

steps.title: Story of יוסף הכהן going to צידן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי supports his view with a story: יוסף הכהן went to his own teacher in צידן, outside ארץ ישראל, to learn תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי said: There was an incident with יוסף הכהן, who went to his teacher in צידן to learn תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי brings a real event to back up his opinion. A כהן left ארץ ישראל and went to צידן to learn from his own teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the background, great teachers such as רבן יוחנן בן זכאי were living in ארץ ישראל at the time. יוסף הכהן still went abroad to his own teacher. This shows in practice that finding the right teacher can justify leaving.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident; a real story brought as precedent
Tzeidan (Sidon), a city outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei said:
There was an incident with Yosef the Kohen
who went to his teacher in Tzeidan
to learn Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּיוֹסֵף הַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוסי's reasoning from step 1 with a historical precedent.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's ruling that a כהן may leave ארץ ישראל to learn from the teacher who suits him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident of יוסף הכהן, who traveled to his teacher in צידן.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי in this dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a specific ruling on this ברייתא: the הלכה is like רבי יוסי. This sets up the גמרא's next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This specific ruling is the key evidence in the sugya. The גמרא is testing רב משרשיא's claim that the general rules of פסק are not accepted. If רבי יוחנן had to rule here specifically, maybe the general rule was not enough.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the dispute in steps 1-2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: a כהן may leave ארץ ישראל to learn תורה from a teacher who suits him.

steps.title: Why did רבי יוחנן need to say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needed a specific ruling here, since he already taught the general rule that in a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this? Didn't you say: between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי, the הלכה is like רבי יוסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling as unnecessary. The general rule should already cover this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the general rule were truly accepted, this specific ruling would be extra. The fact that רבי יוחנן said it suggests the general rule is not reliable. That would support רב משרשיא, who said these rules are not the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this? (why was it stated)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'you' in 'didn't you say' refers to רבי יוחנן himself. The general rule about רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי is one of the rules of פסק attributed to him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the latest attempt to prove רב משרשיא right. An 'extra' ruling would show that the general rule was not trusted.

phrases.english: And why do I need this?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמְרַתְּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי —
phrases.english: But didn't you say: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei —
the halacha is like Rabbi Yosei!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 3 was necessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's specific ruling like רבי יוסי, and with it the reliability of the general rules of פסק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the general rule (רבי יהודה vs. רבי יוסי → follow רבי יוסי) were accepted, a specific ruling would be extra. So its existence suggests the rule is not accepted, as רב משרשיא claimed.

steps.title: אביי: the ruling was needed for a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the specific ruling was needed. We might have thought the general rule applies only to disputes in a משנה and not to disputes in a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It was necessary. It could have entered your mind to say: these words apply in a משנה, but in a ברייתא, say no. So he teaches us.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the general rule. רבי יוחנן's ruling was not extra, because it extends the rule to a dispute found in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule might have been limited to disputes in the משנה. This dispute is in a ברייתא, so רבי יוחנן had to tell us that the rule applies here too. The general rule stays standing, and the proof for רב משרשיא falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say (a mistaken first assumption)
These words apply (only in this case)
A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה

phrases.english: Abaye said: It was necessary,
it would have entered your mind to say:
these words apply in a Mishnah,
but in a Baraita — say no.
So he teaches us (that it applies here too).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by showing the ruling was not extra.
steps.terutzResolutionType: איצטריך: the specific ruling extends the general rule to a new setting.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי against רבי יהודה might apply only to disputes in a משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies to disputes in a ברייתא too. רבי יוחנן's ruling teaches this, so the general rule stays accepted.
steps.whatToRemember: A specific ruling that seems extra may be teaching that a general rule reaches further than we thought (here, from משנה to ברייתא).

steps.title: Reinterpreting רב משרשיא: the rules are not universally accepted
steps.stepSummary: Since none of the proofs worked, the גמרא reinterprets רב משרשיא. He meant that these rules of פסק are not accepted by everyone, because רב did not follow them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he said: These rules are not the opinion of everyone, for רב does not hold of these rules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the whole investigation. It explains רב משרשיא's statement in a milder way: the rules of פסק are real, but some authorities, such as רב, did not accept them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each attempt to prove the rules were rejected was answered, so 'these rules are not הלכה' cannot mean they are completely wrong. The new reading is that the rules are not universal. This matches the earlier evidence in the sugya that רב did not rule by them.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what he meant (a reinterpretation)
General rules (here, rules for deciding הלכה)
He does not hold of it

steps.whatToRemember: The rules of פסק (such as רבי יוסי winning against רבי יהודה) were not cancelled. רב משרשיא only meant that not every אמורא accepted them, and רב did not.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that the rules of פסק are invalid. The final reading only says they are disputed, not that they are false.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shapes how later פוסקים use these general rules. They are standard tools, but one should be aware that some authorities did not follow them.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי כְּלָלֵי לָאו דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל נִינְהוּ,
phrases.english: these rules are not the words of everyone,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא רַב לֵית לֵיהּ הָנֵי כְּלָלֵי.
phrases.english: for Rav does not hold of these rules.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָאָמַר: הָנֵי כְּלָלֵי לָאו דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the last proof (steps 3-5) also fails, the גמרא ends its investigation by reinterpreting רב משרשיא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב משרשיא did not reject the rules of פסק outright. He meant they are not universally accepted, since רב did not follow them.

steps.title: A נכרי's objects do not acquire a שבת location
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: objects that belong to a נכרי do not acquire שביתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: objects of a נכרי do not acquire a שבת resting place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from שמואל about objects owned by a נכרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, an object 'acquires שביתה' when שבת begins, and from then on its 2000-אמה limit is measured from that spot. שמואל says a נכרי's objects do not get such a fixed spot. So if they are brought into town, a Jew may carry them 2000 אמה from where they now are.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquire a fixed Shabbat resting place, from which the 2000-אמה limit is measured
The place where something 'rests' when Shabbat begins

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Objects of a non-Jew do not acquire a Shabbat residence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the larger topic of objects acquiring שביתה after the side discussion about rules of פסק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Objects owned by a נכרי do not acquire שביתה.

steps.title: According to whom? Under the רבנן it would be obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion שמואל follows. Under the רבנן his rule would be too obvious to need saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? If you say according to the רבנן, that is obvious! If ownerless objects, which have no owners, do not acquire residence, is there any question about a נכרי's objects, which do have an owner?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which opinion שמואל's rule is based on. It rejects the first option, the רבנן, because the rule would be obvious under their view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that even הפקר objects do not acquire שביתה. They have no owner, which gives them the strongest case for gaining a spot of their own. Objects with an owner have an even weaker case, so this is a simple קל וחומר, and שמואל would have no reason to teach it.

phrases.english: According to whom?
If you say according to the Rabbis, it is obvious!
Now, if ownerless objects,
which have no owners,
do not acquire residence,
then a non-Jew's objects, which do have an owner,
is it even necessary to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which opinion step 7 follows and rules out the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view is שמואל's ruling built on?
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling, if it were following the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if ownerless objects do not acquire שביתה, owned objects surely do not, so the ruling would add nothing.

steps.title: It follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, but only for ownerless objects
steps.stepSummary: שמואל follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי. He teaches that רבי יוחנן בן נורי's rule applies only to ownerless objects, not to objects owned by a נכרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי. The new point is this: when רבי יוחנן בן נורי said objects acquire residence, that applies only to ownerless objects, which have no owners. It does not apply to a non-Jew's objects, which have owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל was speaking according to רבי יוחנן בן נורי, and it explains what new point he is making.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that ownerless objects do acquire שביתה. We might have extended this to a נכרי's objects, since a נכרי has no Shabbat limits of his own. שמואל limits the rule: objects that have an owner, even a נכרי, do not acquire שביתה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי,
phrases.english: Rather, it is according to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri,
and he teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי קוֹנִין שְׁבִיתָה —
phrases.english: granted that Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said they acquire residence,
that applies only to ownerless objects,
which have no owners.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חֶפְצֵי הַנׇּכְרִי, דְּאִית לְהוּ בְּעָלִים — לָא.
phrases.english: But a non-Jew's objects, which have owners, do not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'according to whom' question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי and teaches that his rule covers only ownerless objects.
steps.whatToRemember: This is only the גמרא's first attempt. It places שמואל with רבי יוחנן בן נורי and limits רבי יוחנן בן נורי's rule to ownerless objects. The ברייתא in Steps 10–11 challenges this reading, and Step 12 drops it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. The רבנן say even ownerless objects do NOT acquire שביתה. It is רבי יוחנן בן נורי who says ownerless objects DO, and שמואל limits his view so it does not cover a נכרי's objects.

steps.title: A ברייתא about borrowed utensils and a non-Jew's produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ברייתא. It ends by saying that produce a נכרי brought from outside the תחום may not be moved, which seems to conflict with the Step 9 reading of שמואל as following רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Someone who borrows a utensil from a non-Jew on יום טוב, or someone who lent a utensil to a non-Jew before יום טוב and got it back on יום טוב, and utensils and storage bins that rested inside the town's limit, may all be moved 2000 אמה in every direction. But if a non-Jew brought him produce from outside the limit, he may not move it from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge שמואל. This step lays out the source, and the attack built on it will follow in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first cases, the utensils were resting inside the town's תחום when יום טוב began, so they may be moved 2000 אמה in every direction from there. The last case is the key one. Produce a נכרי brought from outside the תחום may not be moved at all, which implies that the produce acquired שביתה out there even though it belonged to a נכרי. That seems to contradict the Step 9 reading, in which רבי יוחנן בן נורי excludes a נכרי's objects.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a תנאי source)

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׁוֹאֵל כְּלִי מִן הַנׇּכְרִי בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One who borrows a utensil from a non-Jew on a Festival,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הַמַּשְׁאִיל לוֹ לַנׇּכְרִי כְּלִי מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
phrases.english: and likewise one who lent a non-Jew a utensil on the eve of a Festival
and he returned it to him on the Festival,
and utensils and storage bins that rested within the limit:

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהֶן אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכׇל רוּחַ.
phrases.english: they have two thousand cubits in every direction.

phrases.aramaic: וְנׇכְרִי שֶׁהֵבִיא לוֹ פֵּירוֹת מִחוּץ לַתְּחוּם —
phrases.english: But a non-Jew who brought him produce from outside the limit:
he may not move it from its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to challenge the ruling explained in steps 7–9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Step 9 explanation that שמואל follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, and that רבי יוחנן בן נורי's rule excludes a נכרי's objects
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids moving a נכרי's produce brought from outside the תחום, which implies that a נכרי's objects acquire שביתה. Only רבי יוחנן בן נורי could hold this, so the Step 9 reading, in which he excludes a נכרי's objects, leaves the ברייתא with no author.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits no one under our reading of רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that a נכרי's objects acquire שביתה, the ברייתא matches him. If he holds they do not, the ברייתא matches neither him nor the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say that רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that a נכרי's objects acquire שביתה. Then whose view is this ברייתא? It is רבי יוחנן בן נורי's. But if you say that רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that a נכרי's objects do not acquire שביתה, then whose view is this ברייתא? It is neither רבי יוחנן בן נורי's nor the רבנן's!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the full force of the challenge it raised from the ברייתא in Step 10. Under the reading from Step 9, that ברייתא matches no known opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that even ownerless objects do not acquire שביתה, so a נכרי's objects certainly would not. Only רבי יוחנן בן נורי could say that a נכרי's produce is limited by a תחום. If we say, as Step 9 did, that he limits his rule to ownerless objects, the ברייתא has no author left.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say… (sets up 'this option works, but the other doesn't')
They acquire a 'resting place' (a home base) for שבת, which limits where they can be moved

phrases.english: It works well if you say
that Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri holds
that a non-Jew's objects acquire a resting place,

phrases.aramaic: הָא מַנִּי — רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי הִיא.
phrases.english: then whose is this ברייתא? It is Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri's.
But if you say
that Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri holds
that a non-Jew's objects do not acquire a resting place,
then whose is this ברייתא?

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי וְלָא רַבָּנַן!
phrases.english: It is neither Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri's nor the Rabbis'!
phrases.notes: The ברייתא would have no author.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in Step 10 by showing why the ברייתא conflicts with the reading from Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Step 9 claim that רבי יוחנן בן נורי's rule excludes a נכרי's objects, which was used to explain שמואל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only רבי יוחנן בן נורי could be the author of a ברייתא that limits a נכרי's produce. If he excludes a נכרי's objects, the ברייתא has no author.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי includes a נכרי's objects, and שמואל follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes its approach. רבי יוחנן בן נורי does hold that a נכרי's objects acquire שביתה. שמואל's ruling follows the רבנן instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that a נכרי's objects acquire שביתה. And שמואל ruled according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by dropping the Step 9 explanation. The ברייתא now fits רבי יוחנן בן נורי, and שמואל is placed with the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer removes the problem with the ברייתא. However, it brings back the objection from Step 8: under the רבנן, שמואל's rule seems too obvious to say. The גמרא will deal with that in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (introduces the true position after a challenge)
According to the Sages (the majority view)

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
phrases.english: Really, Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri holds
that a non-Jew's objects acquire a resting place,
and Shmuel ruled according to the Rabbis,

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by rejecting the Step 9 explanation and assigning שמואל to the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the author: שמואל is moved from רבי יוחנן בן נורי to the רבנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who limits his rule to ownerless objects.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן בן נורי includes a נכרי's objects. שמואל follows the רבנן.

steps.title: Why שמואל needed to say it: we might have thought there was a גזירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the 'too obvious' objection. We might have thought the חכמים made a גזירה on a נכרי's objects because of a Jew's objects, so שמואל teaches that there is no such גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you said that under the רבנן this is obvious. You might have thought there is a גזירה on a נכרי's objects because of a Jew's objects. So שמואל teaches us that there is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now answers the old objection from Step 8, that under the רבנן שמואל's rule is too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By basic law, a נכרי's objects do not acquire שביתה under the רבנן. Still, one might think the חכמים would treat them as if they did, so that people would not get careless with a Jew's objects, which really are limited. שמואל's point is that the חכמים made no such גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: And regarding what you said (brings back an earlier objection)
A rabbinic protective decree on one case because of another case
It teaches us (the new point being made)

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not adding a new limitation. He is telling us there is NO גזירה, so a נכרי's objects stay free of שביתה.

phrases.english: And regarding what you said: according to the Rabbis it is obvious,
you might have said:
there is a decree regarding non-Jewish owners
because of Jewish owners,
so he teaches us that there is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the Step 12 answer against the Step 8 'obvious' objection that it brought back.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the ruling teaches something new by ruling out a possible גזירה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים decreed that a נכרי's objects acquire שביתה, as a safeguard for a Jew's objects.
steps.terutzMaskana: No גזירה was made. A נכרי's objects do not acquire שביתה.
steps.whatToRemember: Final position for שמואל: he follows the רבנן. A נכרי's objects do not acquire שביתה, and the חכמים made no גזירה because of a Jew's objects.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules that a נכרי's objects do acquire שביתה, because of a גזירה
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין reports that רבי יוחנן ruled the opposite of שמואל. A נכרי's objects acquire שביתה because of the גזירה made for the sake of a Jew's objects.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a נכרי's objects acquire שביתה. This is a גזירה on a נכרי's objects because of a Jew's objects.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a competing ruling from רבי יוחנן. It directly disagrees with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exact גזירה that שמואל rejected, רבי יוחנן accepts. So the question is not about basic law. It is about whether the חכמים made this safeguard.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a clear dispute between שמואל and רבי יוחנן about whether the חכמים decreed שביתה for a נכרי's objects.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rav Chiya bar Avin said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
A non-Jew's objects acquire a resting place,
as a decree regarding non-Jewish owners
because of Jewish owners.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opinion opposed to שמואל's ruling as it was just explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נכרי's objects acquire שביתה, by rabbinic גזירה, because of a Jew's objects.

steps.title: רבא permits מחוזא residents to buy the rams
steps.stepSummary: Rams were brought to מברכתא on שבת, and רבא allowed the people of מחוזא to buy them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some rams were brought to מברכתא. רבא allowed the people of מחוזא to buy them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that tests the dispute between שמואל and רבי יוחנן. רבא gives a lenient ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rams belonged to non-Jews and were brought from outside the תחום on שבת. The people of מחוזא wanted to buy them and take them home to מחוזא. Allowing this assumes the rams have no שביתה of their own, which is שמואל's view.

phrases.english: Those rams that came to Mavrakhta,
phrases.notes: They were brought on שבת, from outside the תחום.

phrases.english: Rava permitted the people of Mechoza
to buy from them.
phrases.notes: They would take the rams home to מחוזא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a practical case that applies the שמואל / רבי יוחנן dispute from Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא permitted the people of מחוזא to buy the rams that a נכרי brought to מברכתא.

steps.title: רבינא asks for רבא's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רבא whether his ruling relies on שמואל, who said a נכרי's objects do not acquire שביתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: What is your reasoning? Is it because רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל that a נכרי's objects do not acquire שביתה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pins down the source of רבא's ruling. This step sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא recognizes that the only way to permit the rams is through שמואל's view. Once the ruling is tied to שמואל, it can be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquire a Shabbat 'resting place' that limits where they may be moved

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava:
What is your reasoning?
Is it because Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
A gentile's objects do not acquire residence?
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's ruling, discussed earlier in the sugya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the source behind רבא's ruling in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבא's ruling relies on שמואל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is implied that it does, which leads to the challenge in Step 17.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן, not שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רבא. In disputes between שמואל and רבי יוחנן, the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן, and he holds that a נכרי's objects do acquire שביתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when שמואל and רבי יוחנן argue, the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן. And רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a נכרי's objects acquire שביתה. This is a גזירה for a non-Jewish owner because of a Jewish owner.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רבא's ruling. It follows the opinion we do not rule like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule of deciding: when שמואל and רבי יוחנן disagree, we follow רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן said (Step 14) that a נכרי's objects acquire שביתה because of a גזירה. So rams brought from outside the תחום may not be taken to מחוזא.

keyTerms.meaning: The final ruling follows רבי יוחנן
Because of, for fear of confusion with

phrases.english: But regarding Shmuel and Rabbi Yochanan —
the halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan,
phrases.notes: A general rule for deciding the הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and Rav Chiya bar Avin said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
phrases.notes: This is the statement quoted in Step 14.

phrases.english: A gentile's objects acquire residence,
a decree regarding a gentile owner
because of a Jewish owner?!
phrases.notes: People might confuse the two cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא שְׁמוּאֵל וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source identified in Step 16 by applying the rule for deciding between שמואל and רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling allowing the people of מחוזא to buy the rams.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling depends on שמואל. But the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן, who says a נכרי's objects acquire שביתה.

steps.title: רבא retracts: only מברכתא residents may buy
steps.stepSummary: רבא changes his ruling. The rams may be sold only to the people of מברכתא, because for the rams the whole town counts like four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then said: Let the rams be sold to the people of מברכתא. For the rams, all of מברכתא is considered like four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts the challenge and gives a new, stricter ruling. The people of מחוזא may not buy the rams, but the people of מברכתא may.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rams acquired שביתה, and they were taken outside their תחום. Normally that means they may be moved only four אמות. But the whole town where they ended up counts as four אמות for them, so they may be moved anywhere inside מברכתא. Taking them to מחוזא is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Four אמות, the limited space allowed for something taken outside its תחום
It is considered like four אמות

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן: a נכרי's objects acquire שביתה. Rams brought from outside the תחום may be used only within the town they reached, which counts like four אמות for them. They may not be taken to another town.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the rams have no limits. They are limited, but the entire town of מברכתא is treated as their four אמות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the practical outcome of ruling like רבי יוחנן. It also shows that the town where the objects ended up counts as their four אמות.

phrases.english: Rava reconsidered and said:
Let them be sold to the people of Mavrakhta,
phrases.notes: Not to the people of מחוזא.

phrases.english: for all of Mavrakhta, for them,
is considered like four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא accepts the challenge of Step 17 and changes his ruling from Step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Following רבי יוחנן, the rams acquired שביתה. They may be bought only by the people of מברכתא, since the whole town counts as four אמות for them.

steps.title: רבי חייא's teaching about a ditch between two תחומי שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches a ברייתא: a חרם (water-filled ditch) lying between two תחומי שבת requires something. The sentence is completed on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: a water-filled ditch that lies between two Shabbat boundaries requires...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new teaching from רבי חייא about a ditch of water that sits between the שבת boundaries of two towns. It is setting up the case, and the next passage will tell us what this situation requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps dealt with objects, like a נכרי's rams, and where they may be moved on שבת. Now the גמרא brings a similar question about water sitting in a ditch shared between two תחומי שבת. The word 'צריך' tells us some action or barrier is needed, but the sentence is cut off here, so we wait for the next passage to learn exactly what.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught. It introduces a ברייתא, a teaching from the era of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself.
Here, a ditch or pool filled with water
The שבת boundaries: the area around a town, usually 2000 אמות, in which a person or object may be moved on שבת
Requires. Something must be done. The text continues on the next amud.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the teaching ends at 'צריך'. The sentence is incomplete here. What is required is stated on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya taught (a baraita):
phrases.notes: Attribution formula introducing a ברייתא. It is merged into this step.

phrases.english: A water-filled ditch that is between two Shabbat boundaries requires...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud with what is required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's final ruling on the rams (Step 18), the גמרא brings a related ברייתא about water located between two תחומי שבת. It continues the larger theme of where things may be moved on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרם lying between two תחומי שבת requires something. The specific requirement is stated on the next amud.
